problem: Embodied mobile robots struggle to navigate accurately in unseen environments from language instructions; prior VLN models do not combine global topological planning with local visual planning well.
motivation: Generalization to unseen environments is the key bottleneck for VLN. Global map-level reasoning and local observation-level reasoning are complementary, so fusing them should improve success and reduce navigation error.
key_idea: Encode instructions with pre-trained BERT and use a dual-scale transformer action predictor (global topological-graph predictor plus local predictor) whose outputs are dynamically fused into the final action.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation evidence can be cited. The abstract implies that combining global topological planning with local visual planning through dynamic fusion improves generalization to unseen environments.
method: Instruction encoder: pre-trained BERT extracts contextual representations of the natural language instruction.
Global predictor: uses a topological graph for high-level scene information and global action planning, with transformer-based cross-modal fusion.
Local predictor: attends only to visual information around the current position for local action planning, with transformer-based cross-modal fusion.
Dynamic fusion: combines the outputs of the global and local predictors into the final robot action.

setting.backbone: BERT + transformer cross-modal action predictors (global and local)
setting.training_data: not stated in abstract (presumably standard VLN training data in the Matterport3D simulator)

results: The abstract claims a higher navigation success rate and a lower mean navigation error than previous work in the Matterport3D simulator, with no numbers or named baselines given.
